source.title: Comparing Normalization Methods for Limited Batch Size Segmentation Neural Networks
source.authors: M. Kolarík; Radim Burget; K. Říha

record.file_problem: None noted; the supplied text contains the paper through its references.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how normalization choice affects training and segmentation outcomes for a 3D res-U-Net on a medical segmentation dataset, an extension beyond the claim versions’ specified benchmarks and tasks.
record.gate_note: Reports separately the Dice scores for no normalization, BatchNorm, five GroupNorm group counts, and InstanceNorm, plus epoch and prediction times. These are included because they are results of the tested normalization conditions. No training classification error is reported. The comparison does not test random or corrupted labels, width, initialization, shortcut removal, or learning-rate stability.
record.test_reason: The study compares final segmentation Dice, time per epoch and prediction time. It does not measure accuracy-gain speed, time to matched accuracy or higher learning-rate tolerance, so its normalization comparison does not test V6. Its own results do not test V1–V5 either.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase accurately attributes the authors' conclusion: InstanceNorm achieved the highest Dice, 0.96, at batch size 1, comparable to their earlier, more complex network. The abstract also calls its implementation computationally efficient relative to no normalization, but Table 1 shows longer epochs (163 versus 131 seconds) and equal prediction time (8 seconds).
record.recipe_differences: Compares normalization methods in a 3D medical segmentation task using a 3D res-u-net and Dice coefficient; it does not use the claim versions’ classification-error benchmarks or training setups.
record.method_sensitivity: Final Dice differs across normalization method and GroupNorm group count; timing also differs by method.

fits_no_version.finding: After 30 epochs at batch size 1, Dice was 0.598 without normalization, 0.888 with BatchNorm, 0.916–0.941 with GroupNorm and 0.960 with InstanceNorm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization choice affects final segmentation quality in this 3D res-U-Net recipe, with InstanceNorm achieving the highest Dice.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report divergence during unnormalized training with their chosen loss and learning rate, without a learning-rate sweep or stability-threshold measurement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The unnormalized network failed to converge well under this particular training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalization implementations differ in epoch and inference costs; InstanceNorm takes 163 versus 131 seconds per epoch without normalization, while both have 8-second prediction times.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization implementation affects computational overhead independently of convergence speed.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Telecommunications and Signal Processing
record.problems: One dataset comprising 10 healthy subjects; no uncertainty estimates are reported. Training runs use 30 epochs and one learning rate. The results measure segmentation Dice, not classification training error. The paper notes that the no-normalization model diverged under the chosen loss and learning rate.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR, corrupted or random labels, and model-size or regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, plain-versus-shortcut comparisons, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent training speed, trainable depth and signal or gradient propagation.
Stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence across learning rates.
Faster accuracy gains with BatchNorm, higher learning-rate tolerance and comparable training speed or stability using Fixup. Only one learning rate and final Dice are reported.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the proposed V6 limits_scope verdict: unmeasured training acceleration and learning-rate tolerance are untested, rather than evidence limiting the claim. Dice evaluation is not identified clearly as training, validation or test performance.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR benchmark, training classification error, random or corrupted labels, or model-size comparison.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or neuron-width comparison.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison; all tested networks use the stated 3D res-U-Net architecture.
No initialization comparison or signal/gradient propagation measurement.
No learning-rate-above-stability experiment, curvature measurement, or divergence threshold comparison.

Tests normalization effects only on one 3D segmentation network with batch size 1. It does not test accuracy-gain speed, learning-rate tolerance, the specified MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet settings, or Fixup.

rows.operation_detail: Trained 30 epochs with batch size 1 and the reported loss and learning rate, without normalization.

conditions.value: binary spine segmentation from 3D CT scans

rows.note: Authors say this network did not converge to a good solution, partly due to the BCeDice loss function.
rows.check: Dice 0.598 is correctly transcribed, but final segmentation quality does not measure V6's training acceleration. Reported divergence under this recipe does not establish comparative learning-rate tolerance.
